tabs_ne.check: पहिले नजिकको कृषि प्राविधिकलाई सोध्नुहोस्। नजिकै मसुरको बीउ पाइन्छ कि सोध्नुहोस्। छिमेकीलाई मसुर कहिले रोप्छन् भनी सोध्नुहोस्। यहाँ मसुर राम्रो हुन्छ कि सोध्नुहोस्। धानअघि ढैंचा लगाउने बारे सोध्नुहोस्। नार्क: ‘धानका लागि लोकप्रिय हरियो मल बाली’ (अनुवाद)। लाभ: ‘५०–१०० किलो रासायनिक मलको N बराबर’ (अनुवाद)। पुस्तिकाले लाक्सिना र अरू (१९८७) लाई उद्धृत गर्छ। पुस्तिका: अधिकारी, नार्क २०१४, लुम्बिनी कृषि वेबसाइट। यो यहाँ मिल्छ कि, कृषि कार्यालयलाई सोध्नुहोस्। तपाईंसँग साँच्चै कति पानी छ, जाँच्नुहोस्। पहिले एउटा सानो भागमा मात्र गरेर हेर्नुहोस्। आफ्नो जमिन तपाईंलाई नै राम्रो थाहा छ।

The range spans the lowest to highest.

en: We tested two ways with satellite rain.
Neither could show a change in timing.
In 2017, rain gauges stopped feeding it.
After that, its rain is not steady.
So we use Nepal's official monsoon record.
No clear change since 2001, in Nepal's weather office records.
Both satellite rain checks show no clear change.
These records share some rain gauges.
ne: हामीले भू-उपग्रहको वर्षाबाट दुई तरिका जाँच्यौं।
कुनैले पनि समयको फरक देखाउन सकेन।
सन् २०१७ मा वर्षा मापन केन्द्रको जानकारी रोकियो।
त्यसैले हामी नेपाल सरकारको आधिकारिक मनसुन अभिलेख हेर्छौं।
नेपालको मौसम कार्यालयको अभिलेखमा सन् २००१ यता स्पष्ट फरक छैन।
भू-उपग्रहका दुवै वर्षा जाँचमा पनि स्पष्ट फरक देखिँदैन।
यी अभिलेखले केही वर्षा मापन केन्द्र साझा गर्छन्।

onset.caveat: DHM's date is the day the monsoon enters Nepal in the east. It reaches Kathmandu a few days later.

words.en: NASA's rain maps are checked against rain gauges. Around this field, gauge reports stopped in 2017. Before, the gauges set almost all of it. After, the picture from space took over. Its yearly rain here jumped to 2730 mm. Before, it was 1840 mm. The nearest town's usual rain: 1380 mm. We scaled each month from 2017 back down. Each month now matches its earlier years. We tested this on years we kept aside. Monthly error at the airport: 94 mm before. After our fix: 31 mm. This fix may also hide real change. So we show both, as a range.
words.ne: नासाको वर्षाको नक्सा वर्षा मापकसँग जाँचिन्छ। यो खेत वरिपरि २०१७ देखि मापकका नाप आएनन्। पहिले, वर्षाको नाप लगभग सबै मापकबाटै आउँथ्यो। त्यसपछि, अन्तरिक्षबाट हेरेको नापले ठाउँ लियो। यहाँको वार्षिक वर्षा २७३० मिलिमिटर पुग्यो। पहिले यो १८४० मिलिमिटर थियो। नजिकको सहरको सामान्य वर्षा: १३८० मिलिमिटर। हामीले २०१७ देखिको हरेक महिनाको वर्षा घटायौं। अब हरेक महिना पहिलेका वर्षसँग मिल्छ। यो जाँच अलग राखेका वर्षमा गर्‍यौं। विमानस्थलमा मासिक फरक: पहिले ९४ मिलिमिटर। सुधारपछि: ३१ मिलिमिटर। यस सुधारले साँचो फेरबदल पनि लुकाउन सक्छ। त्यसैले हामी दुवै देखाउँछौं, दायराका रूपमा।

words.en: We tried teaching a computer this field's habits. It learned from 24 seasons seen from space. We tested it on years it never saw. It did not beat our simple water count. So we left it out. It looks at greenness, not at the harvest.
words.ne: हामीले कम्प्युटरलाई यो खेतको बानी सिकाउन खोज्यौं। यसले अन्तरिक्षबाट देखिएका २४ बाली याममा सिक्यो। हामीले यसलाई नदेखेका वर्षमा जाँच्यौं। यसले हाम्रो सरल पानीको हिसाबलाई जित्न सकेन। त्यसैले हामीले यसलाई राखेनौं। यसले हरियाली हेर्छ, उब्जनी होइन।

choices.choice: Structure of the rain-fed transplanting rules in Balwinder-Singh et al. 2019, Field Crops Research 239:92-103, sec. 2.3.2 (APSIM, Bihar: seedlings 'at least 21 days old', transplanting when 'surface water ponding exceeded 50 mm', no crop 'if these conditions were not met by 15 August') and Han, Montes, Hussain & Krupnik 2024, Climatic Change 177:77 (DSSAT, Bangladesh: transplanting when a 'threshold ponding water depth (30 mm) was reached by rainfall'). A rain total stands in for the ponding depth because the twin has no pond for rain-fed paddy (METHOD_NOTES 2). Claude's reading, fixed before the run; owner-approved 2026-11-14 ('4c: yes, apply the sourced rain-fed rice rule')
choices.value: a RAIN-FED paddy is transplanted on the first day, on or after its planned day, by which the rain since prep_days before the planned day (the nursery's sowing) reaches prep_mm (soaking and puddling); later than max_delay_days after the planned day the season fails: harvest 0 (the field is left fallow or the seedlings are lost). A late paddy is simulated from its actual day as the same plain bucket; a later crop that would overlap moves to the day after it ends. No extra loss per day of delay. Irrigated paddy is unchanged

If they do, leave them off and record why.' The 0.05 margin is Claude's choice, fixed before the comparison: smaller changes are within the rounding of the published checks

If any is worse, the losses stay off and why is recorded

choices.choice: FAO Training Manual 4 (1989), sec. 4.4, Step 5: 'The percolation and seepage losses depend on the type of soil. They will be low in very heavy, well-puddled clay soils and high in the case of more sandy soils. They can best be determined locally. If no local data can be obtained, the following values may be used: for heavy clay: PERC = 2 mm/day = 60 mm/month; for more sandy soils: PERC = 8 mm/day = 240 mm/month; on average: PERC = 5 mm/day = 150 mm/month'. The demo's topsoil is loam (VALIDATION 2.5), neither heavy clay nor sandy, so the 'average' value. (Manual 3, 1986, sec. 4.4, Step 5: heavy clay 4, sandy 8, average 6 mm/day.) Reading 'this soil type' as FAO's average class is Claude's choice, fixed before the first run; put to the owner
choices.status: Claude's choice, put to the owner

choices.choice: FAO's PERC is the loss of a flooded field ('A water layer is established ... and maintained throughout the growing season. The amount of water needed for maintaining the water layer has already been taken into account with the determination of the percolation and seepage losses', Manual 3, Step 6); the bucket has no water above field capacity (METHOD_NOTES 2), so 'at field capacity' stands for flooded or saturated. Manual 4, sec. 4.2: 'Puddling reduces the permeability of the soil and therefore also reduces the percolation losses'. Claude's reading, fixed before the first run; put to the owner
choices.value: a paddy day is wet when its root zone starts the day at field capacity (every ponded day, after the morning top-up) or the day's rain, less runoff, brings it back to field capacity. On a wet day perc_mm_day leaves the field: first out of the water above field capacity, which the bucket drains anyway (that deep percolation is counted as seepage and percolation, so no water is counted twice), the rest out of the root zone; at the wilting point the loss gives way first. A day that starts below field capacity and is not refilled loses nothing
choices.status: Claude's choice, put to the owner

choices.choice: FAO Training Manual 4, sec. 4.4, Step 6: 'Sometimes a water layer of 100 mm is established after transplant and maintained throughout the growing season. In other cases the water layer is reduced to 20 to 50 mm ...'. Claude's choice, stated before the first run
choices.value: not modelled: FAO's 100-mm water layer (Manual 4, sec. 4.4, Step 6) is water held above the soil, a store the bucket has no room for (METHOD_NOTES 2); keeping it up is inside perc_mm_day (Step 6, quoted above). So a watered paddy's irrigation is short by up to 100 mm a season, and a rain-fed paddy's rain above field capacity is lost the same day instead of being held by the bunds

choices.choice: Claude's choice (the coordinator's, 2026-11-14 afternoon), fixed before its first run; put to the owner. Why: Bouman, Barker, Humphreys, Tuong et al. (2007), 'Rice: feeding the billions', ch. 14 of Water for Food, Water for Life (IWMI/Earthscan), p. 523: 'Though runoff, seepage, and percolation are losses at the field level, they are often captured and reused downstream and do not necessarily lead to true water depletion at the irrigation area or basin scales. However, the proportion and magnitude of reuse of these flows are not generally known'; p. 526: 'Percolation from rice fields, canals, and storage reservoirs recharges groundwater systems'. Perry, Steduto & Karajeh (2017), Does improved irrigation technology save water? A review of the evidence (FAO, Cairo; ISBN 978-92-5-109774-8), p. 8: 'percolation from “inefficient” irrigation ... is often a major source of aquifer recharge'. Whether this valley's percolation is reused is not known (diary.groundwater is falling, so the score is already made stricter: plans.water_strict_when_falling); that is why the losses stay visible
choices.value: with the losses on, the plans' water score (plans/score.water_score) counts the crop's own water need: the watered case's irrigation less irrigation_losses_mm. irrigation_losses_mm = the pond top-ups that replace the previous day's seepage and percolation (each top-up less what the crop alone used beyond that day's rain, so the first top-up of a season is the crop's) + the land-preparation water (watered_case). It is reported beside irrigation_mm in the seasons, the years and the plans, never hidden. With the losses off nothing changes

tabs_ne.benefits: उब्जनी: ५ सम्म बढी, वा उस्तै। अहिलेभन्दा कम पानी चाहिन्छ। मसुरले माटोमा प्राकृतिक मल थप्छ। बाली फेर्दा कीरा र रोग घट्न सक्छ।
tabs_ne.unknown: यो नमुना खेत हो, तपाईंको होइन। नजिकका भागहरूको माटोको नक्सा एउटै छ। सबै भागमा एउटै वर्षा र मौसम मानिएको छ। रोप्ने मिति सामान्य हुन्, तपाईंका होइनन्। तपाईंको हिउँदे बालीको मिति हाम्रोभन्दा फरक हुन सक्छ। यहाँ जरा कति गहिरो पुग्छ, थाहा छैन। त्यसैले उब्जनीको बढोत्तरी एउटा दायरामा छ। धान र मसुरमा तिर्खाको असर हाम्रो अनुमान हो। पानी लगाउन सक्नुहुन्छ भने धान पानीमा रहन्छ। पानी नभए धान वर्षामा मात्र भर पर्छ। पानीको स्रोत थाहा नभएकाले दुवै देखाएका छौं। नासाले आफ्नो वर्षाको नाप जमिनका वर्षा मापकसँग मिलाउँछ। यहाँ नजिकका मापकबाट २०१७ देखि नाप आएनन्। त्यसपछि यहाँ नासाको वर्षा धेरै बढी देखियो। हामीले २०१७ देखिको वर्षा पहिलेजस्तै हुने गरी घटायौं। यसले साँच्चै भएको फेरबदल पनि लुकाउन सक्छ। हाम्रो वर्षाको नाप अझै बढी हुन सक्छ। जम्मा भएको पानी ठूलो क्षेत्रभरिको नाप हो। यो तपाईंको आफ्नै इनार होइन। हामीले तुषारो परेका रात बढी गनेका हुन सक्छौं। तपाईंको मेहनत र खर्च यसमा गनिएको छैन।
tabs_ne.check: पहिले नजिकको कृषि प्राविधिकलाई सोध्नुहोस्। नजिकै मसुरको बीउ पाइन्छ कि सोध्नुहोस्। छिमेकीलाई मसुर कहिले रोप्छन् भनी सोध्नुहोस्। यहाँ मसुर राम्रो हुन्छ कि सोध्नुहोस्। धानअघि ढैंचा लगाउने बारे सोध्नुहोस्। नार्क: ‘धानका लागि लोकप्रिय हरियो मल बाली’ (अनुवाद)। लाभ: ‘५०–१०० किलो रासायनिक मलको N बराबर’ (अनुवाद)। पुस्तिकाले लाक्सिना र अरू (१९८७) लाई उद्धृत गर्छ। पुस्तिका: अधिकारी, नार्क २०१४, लुम्बिनी कृषि वेबसाइट। यो यहाँ मिल्छ कि, कृषि कार्यालयलाई सोध्नुहोस्। तपाईंसँग साँच्चै कति पानी छ, जाँच्नुहोस्। पहिले एउटा सानो भागमा मात्र गरेर हेर्नुहोस्। आफ्नो जमिन तपाईंलाई नै राम्रो थाहा छ।
